t: Fire programme: net retention ₹25 lakh, 1st surplus 20 lines, 2nd surplus 16 lines, balance facultative. On a risk of sum insured ₹12 crore a claim of ₹60 lakh is paid. The 2nd surplus treaty's share of the claim is
e: 2nd surplus capacity = 16 × ₹25 lakh = ₹4 crore = 4/12 of the risk. Its share of the claim = 4/12 × ₹60 lakh = ₹20 lakh (retention 1.25, 1st surplus 25, facultative 13.75).

t: An insurer's net retention on fire risks is ₹50 lakh. To be able to accept a risk of sum insured ₹9 crore entirely through its surplus treaty without any facultative placement, the treaty must provide at least
e: Surplus capacity required = ₹9 crore − ₹50 lakh retention = ₹8.5 crore. One line = ₹50 lakh, so 8.5/0.5 = 17 lines are needed (treaty capacity = retention × (lines + 1)).

t: A 25% quota share treaty applies to every fire risk; the insurer's net retention after quota share is ₹10 lakh and a 10-line surplus treaty operates on that net retention. On a risk of sum insured ₹1 crore a claim of ₹40 lakh is settled. The ceding insurer's net share of the claim is
e: Quota share takes ₹25 lakh of the SI, net retention ₹10 lakh, surplus ₹65 lakh (within 10 × 10 = ₹1 crore). Claim is shared in the same ratios: QS 10, surplus 26, cedant 10/100 × 40 = ₹4 lakh.

t: An insurer's risk XL programme has a first layer of ₹30 lakh xs ₹20 lakh and a second layer of ₹1 crore xs ₹50 lakh. A single loss of ₹1.2 crore occurs. The second layer reinsurers pay
e: The cedant bears ₹20 lakh, the first layer pays ₹30 lakh (up to ₹50 lakh) and the second layer pays the excess over ₹50 lakh, i.e. ₹70 lakh, within its ₹1 crore limit.

topic: Stop loss - recovery with upper limit
t: A stop loss cover pays 90% of losses in excess of an 80% loss ratio up to a loss ratio of 120%. Premium income is ₹40 crore and losses are ₹52 crore. The recovery is
e: Loss ratio = 130%, but cover ends at 120%. Covered band = 120% − 80% = 40% of ₹40 crore = ₹16 crore; 90% of that = ₹14.4 crore. The cedant bears the 10% co-share and everything above 120%.

t: Facilities (all on PML basis): obligatory cession 4% max ₹5 crore; net retention ₹2 crore; pool cession 20% max ₹4 crore; 1st surplus 10 lines max ₹20 crore. A fire policy for sum insured ₹150 crore is written with PML 20%. The amount to be reinsured facultatively is
e: Amount to reinsure = 20% of ₹150 crore = ₹30 crore. Obligatory 4% = ₹1.2 crore; retention ₹2 crore; pool 20% of 30 = 6 but max ₹4 crore; 1st surplus 10 × 2 = ₹20 crore. Total ₹27.2 crore; balance ₹2.8 crore facultative.

t: Over five years an insurer's GNPI totalled ₹40 crore and losses incurred to its XL layer totalled ₹1.2 crore. The treaty rate is burning cost loaded at 100/75, minimum 3.5% and maximum 6%. Current year GNPI is ₹10 crore. The XL premium is
e: Burning cost = 1.2/40 = 3%; loaded = 3 × 100/75 = 4%, which lies within the 3.5%–6% range. Premium = 4% of ₹10 crore = ₹40 lakh.

topic: Excess of loss premium - maximum rate
t: GNPI ₹6 crore; incurred losses to the XL cover ₹54 lakh; rate 100/70 of burning cost, minimum 5%, maximum 10%. The XL premium chargeable is
e: Burning cost = 54/600 = 9%; loaded = 9 × 100/70 = 12.86%, which exceeds the maximum. Premium is charged at the maximum 10% of ₹6 crore = ₹60 lakh.

t: An XL cover of ₹1 crore xs ₹25 lakh carries an annual premium of ₹5 lakh with two reinstatements at 100% additional premium, pro rata to amount only. Two losses produce recoveries of ₹40 lakh and ₹75 lakh. The total reinstatement premium payable is
e: Reinstatement premium = recovery ÷ limit × annual premium for each loss: 40/100 × 5 lakh = ₹2,00,000 and 75/100 × 5 lakh = ₹3,75,000; total ₹5,75,000.

t: GNPI for four years: ₹200, ₹220, ₹260 and ₹320 lakh; losses to the XL layer: ₹10, ₹15, ₹8 and ₹17 lakh. The pure burning cost is
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Pure burning cost = total losses ÷ total GNPI = 50/1000 = 5%. A loading of 100/70 would give a loaded rate of 7.14%.

topic: Reinstatement premium - pro rata to time (leap year)
t: Treaty period 1.4.2027 to 31.3.2028; cover ₹7.5 lakh xs ₹2.5 lakh; rate 10% on GNPI ₹10 lakh; a ground-up loss of ₹9 lakh occurs on 1.10.2027; one reinstatement at 100% pro rata to amount and time. The reinstatement premium is approximately
In the above cover (recovery ₹6.5 lakh, XL premium ₹1,00,000, reinstatement premium ₹43,333), a reinsurer with a 30% share receives in premium and pays in loss respectively
e: A 30% participant receives 30% of the XL premium (₹30,000) and 30% of the reinstatement premium (₹13,000) and pays 30% of the recovery, ₹1,95,000.

t: A buffer XL of ₹50 lakh xs ₹25 lakh carries an aggregate deductible of 3% of GNPI; GNPI is ₹5 crore. Ground-up losses: ₹30 lakh, ₹40 lakh and ₹60 lakh. Reinsurers pay in total
e: Aggregate deductible = ₹15 lakh. Excess over ₹25 lakh: 5, 15 and 35 = ₹55 lakh. The first ₹15 lakh (5 + 10) is absorbed by the aggregate deductible; reinsurers pay 5 + 35 = ₹40 lakh.

t: A cat XL cover of ₹50 lakh xs ₹20 lakh has one reinstatement at 100%. A cyclone (one occurrence) causes a loss of ₹1 crore and a later flood causes ₹45 lakh. The total recovery under the cover for the year is
e: Cyclone: ₹80 lakh above priority, limited to ₹50 lakh, which exhausts the cover; the limit is reinstated once. Flood: ₹45 − 20 = ₹25 lakh paid from the reinstated limit. Total ₹75 lakh.

t: Treaty account (100%): premium ₹8,00,000; portfolio premium entry ₹2,00,000; portfolio loss entry ₹50,000; commission 35%; taxes ₹16,000; claims paid ₹3,10,000; premium reserve retained 40%; XL premium for common account ₹6,000; common account XL recoveries ₹9,000. The balance due to a reinsurer with a 25% share is

A treaty in its first year shows: premium ₹20 lakh, commission 30%, claims paid ₹9 lakh, outstanding claims ₹2 lakh, management expenses 5%, clean-cut portfolio withdrawal at 40% of premium and 90% of outstanding losses. Profit commission at 20% is
o: nil, as the statement shows a loss of ₹5.8 lakh
e: Outgo = commission 6 + claims 9 + ME 1 + premium withdrawal 8 + loss withdrawal 1.8 = ₹25.8 lakh against income ₹20 lakh. No portfolio entry arises in the first year. Result is a loss, so no profit commission is payable.

topic: Profit commission - with interest on reserves
t: Treaty year: premium ₹100 lakh; portfolio entry premium ₹35 lakh and loss ₹20 lakh; commission 30%; management expenses 5%; claims paid ₹30 lakh; premium reserve retained 40%; loss reserve retained 100% of outstanding ₹25 lakh; interest at 5% on both reserves retained. Profit commission at 20% is
Premium ceded ₹1.2 crore; net adjusted profit ₹15 lakh; profit commission 20% on profit up to 10% of premium and 75% on the balance. Total profit commission is
e: 10% of premium = ₹12 lakh → 20% = ₹2.4 lakh. Balance profit ₹3 lakh → 75% = ₹2.25 lakh. Total ₹4.65 lakh.

t: A treaty provides profit commission at 20% with losses carried forward until extinguished. Year 1 shows a loss of ₹6 lakh; year 2 shows a profit of ₹10 lakh. Profit commission for year 2 is
e: The year-1 deficit is set against year-2 profit: 10 − 6 = ₹4 lakh. Profit commission = 20% of ₹4 lakh = ₹80,000.

topic: Catastrophe XL - rate on line and payback
t: A cat XL layer of ₹80 crore is bought for a premium of ₹4 crore. The payback period implied by this pricing is
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Rate on line = 4/80 = 5%; payback period = 1 ÷ rate on line = 20 years, i.e. one full-limit loss is expected to be recouped over 20 years of premium.

t: Losses paid during the year ₹1,50,000; outstanding losses carried forward ₹60,000; outstanding losses brought forward ₹35,000. Incurred losses for the year are
e: Incurred losses = paid + outstanding at end − outstanding at beginning = 1,50,000 + 60,000 − 35,000 = ₹1,75,000.

t: Reinsurance is the insurance of the risk assumed by
e: Reinsurance is a contract under which the reinsurer indemnifies the insurer (cedant) for part or all of the liability the insurer has assumed under policies issued by it.

t: A catastrophe excess of loss cover protects the insurer against
o: an increase in the overall loss ratio
a series of unrelated losses during the policy period
a single large loss on one risk
unknown accumulation of losses arising out of one event
e: Cat XL responds to the aggregate of individual losses arising from one event (storm, earthquake, flood) which exceed the per-event retention.

t: Aviation reinsurance
o: uses all forms of reinsurance protection
is not reinsured because of pooling
e: Because of the size and accumulation of aviation exposures, proportional treaties, facultative placements and excess of loss covers are all used.

topic: Retention - per risk and per event
t: The per-risk retention is derived from the per-event retention by
o: multiplying it by the number of risks in the portfolio
dividing it by the probable maximum number of individual risks involved in one event
e: Retention per risk = retention per event ÷ PMN (probable maximum number of risks hit by one event), so that the accumulation from one event stays within the event retention.

t: The obligatory cession to the Indian reinsurer was reduced from 20% to 15% in
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Statutory cession: 20% until 2006-07, 15% in 2007-08, 10% from 2008-09, 5% from 2013-14 and 4% from 2022-23.

t: The format of annual accounts of reinsurance companies in India is governed by
o: the Insurance Act, 1938 and the IRDA Act, 1999
e: Insurers and reinsurers prepare accounts in the formats prescribed by the regulator under the Insurance Act, 1938 read with the IRDA Act, 1999, in addition to company law requirements.

t: After a reinsurance agreement has been duly stamped and found in order it is
o: signed in triplicate, one copy for the regulator
signed in duplicate, one stamped copy being returned to the other party
e: The agreement is scrutinised, stamped, signed in duplicate and the stamped counterpart is exchanged; addenda must also be stamped.

t: A joint underwriting operation in which participants assume a predetermined and fixed interest in all business written is a
e: A pool shares premiums, losses and expenses in agreed fixed ratios among its members, e.g. the terrorism or nuclear pools.

t: Burning cost is the ratio of
o: actual past losses to the corresponding premium for the same period
e: Burning cost expresses the losses to the XL layer as a percentage of the subject premium (GNPI) over the experience period; it is the basis for experience rating of working XL covers.

t: A treaty under which the amount reinsured is expressed as lying between a minimum and a maximum quota share is a
e: A variable quota share treaty allows the cession percentage to vary by band of sum insured between an agreed minimum and maximum.

t: Under the usual intermediary clause, payment of premium by the cedant to the broker
o: is not a payment to the reinsurer until the reinsurer receives it
is deemed to be payment to the reinsurer
must be matched by a bank guarantee
e: The intermediary clause shifts the credit risk of the broker to the reinsurers: cedant's payments to the intermediary are deemed received by the reinsurer, while the reinsurer's payments to the intermediary are not payments to the cedant until actually received.

t: Which of the following is NOT a recognised method of reinsurance commission?
e: Commission under proportional treaties is paid as a flat rate, on a sliding scale linked to loss ratio, or supplemented by profit (contingent) commission; there is no 'sales turnover' commission.

t: Under a sliding scale commission the rate of ceding commission
o: varies inversely with the loss ratio, between a minimum and a maximum
rises as the loss ratio rises
is fixed for the life of the treaty
depends on the volume of gross premium
e: A sliding scale rewards good results: as the loss ratio falls the commission rises, subject to a floor and a ceiling; the scale is not always one-to-one.

t: In surplus reinsurance the term 'line' refers to
o: the premium paid to the reinsurer
the amount ceded to the reinsurer
the number of reinsurers on the slip
the cedant's net retention, which forms the unit of the treaty
e: One line equals the ceding company's retention; the capacity of a surplus treaty is expressed as a number of lines (multiples of the retention).

t: An insurer is required to file with the regulator copies of its treaty slips and excess of loss cover notes for the year within
o: 15 days of the commencement of the financial year
30 days of the commencement of the financial year
60 days of the commencement of the financial year
90 days of the end of the financial year
e: The reinsurance regulations require filing of treaty slips and XL cover notes within 30 days of the commencement of the financial year to which they relate.

t: Which of the following is an example of accumulation of risk?
o: several persons insured under separate PA policies travelling in the same aircraft
a situation where a loss does not exhaust the full sum insured
two policies on the same property with different insurers
e: Accumulation is a concentration of risks that could produce many losses from one event, such as several insureds in one aircraft or many insured properties hit by one windstorm.

t: Deduction for health insurance premium under Section 80D for an individual below 60 years (self and family) is up to:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). ₹25,000; ₹50,000 where the insured is a senior citizen; an additional ₹25,000/₹50,000 for parents.

t: An accumulation control register is most commonly maintained for
e: Catastrophe perils such as earthquake require zone-wise aggregation of sums insured so that per-event retention and cat XL limits can be set.

t: Which of the following is NOT relevant for fixing the retention of a marine cargo account?
o: whether cover is mostly on all-risk or restricted terms
breakdown of premium by age and size of the carrying vessel
e: Age and size of vessel are hull underwriting considerations; cargo retention depends on terms of cover, type of cargo, packing and the spread of exposures.

t: In choosing reinsurers for its programme, a cedant should NOT base its selection on
o: the reinsurer's technical and administrative capability
the quality of the long-term relationship
the cheapest terms available irrespective of security
e: Security of recovery matters more than price; a reinsurer selected only because it is cheapest may fail to pay when a large loss occurs.

t: A cedant arranges facultative reinsurance on a risk even though treaty capacity exists, because it does not wish to expose its treaty reinsurers to that particular hazardous risk. This is
o: a breach of the treaty's reinsuring clause
a legitimate use of facultative reinsurance
permitted only with the regulator's approval
possible only under a fac-oblig treaty
e: Facultative placement is used when additional capacity is needed, when the risk is outside the treaty, or when the cedant prefers not to burden its treaty with a particular risk.

t: A proportional treaty is cancelled on a 'cut-off' basis. For policies that commenced before the cancellation date the reinsurer
o: remains liable until each policy expires
is liable only for outstanding claims already advised
remains liable for a further 12 months
ceases to be liable for losses occurring on or after the cancellation date and normally returns the unearned premium portfolio
e: Under cut-off the reinsurer's liability stops at the cancellation date and the unearned premium portfolio is returned; under run-off the reinsurer stays on risk until natural expiry of each policy.

t: A branch wants to cede to the fire treaty a risk that is specifically excluded by the treaty wording. The reinsurance department should
o: cede it anyway and disclose it in the bordereau
treat it as automatically covered because the treaty is obligatory
seek a special acceptance from the treaty reinsurers before cession
cede it to the obligatory cession only
e: A special acceptance is the facultative extension of a treaty to embrace a risk not automatically included within its terms; without it the excluded risk is not covered.

t: Third-party insurance is compulsory for a motor vehicle used in a public place under which section of the Motor Vehicles Act 1988?
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Section 146 makes TP cover compulsory; Section 164 fixes no-fault compensation (₹5 lakh death / ₹2.5 lakh grievous hurt).

t: A professional indemnity XL treaty is written on a claims-made basis. A negligent act in 2022 is first reported as a claim in 2025. The treaty that responds is
o: the 2022 treaty, when the act occurred
the 2025 treaty, when the claim was reported
neither, as the claim is time-barred
e: Under claims-made the date of the claim report is deemed the loss date, which 'cuts off the tail' for the reinsurer; under an occurrence basis the 2022 treaty would respond.

t: A policy for annual premium ₹12,000 is issued on 1 January. On 31 March the amounts of earned and unearned premium are respectively
e: Written premium ₹12,000 is booked at issue; three of twelve months have expired, so earned premium is ₹3,000 and unearned premium (reserve for unexpired risk) is ₹9,000.

t: Under the loss advice clause of a proportional treaty, the cedant must specially advise the reinsurer of a loss when
o: any loss, however small, is intimated
only after the loss is paid
the loss reaches an agreed amount, with outstanding losses advised at anniversary dates
e: Losses are normally passed through the accounts; a separate advice is required when a loss reaches the agreed advice limit, and outstanding losses are reported at anniversary dates.

t: A premium bordereau sent to the reinsurer under a proportional treaty would normally show
o: a detailed list of claims paid
a detailed list of policies ceded with particulars such as the insured's address, sum insured, period and reinsurance premium
the reinsurer's share of outstanding claims
e: The premium bordereau lists each risk ceded (insured, location, sum insured, period, premium, amount and premium reinsured); the loss bordereau lists each loss affecting reinsured risks.

t: A cedant decides to start writing a new hazardous class under the fire treaty without informing the reinsurers. This conflicts with the
e: The change of underwriting policy clause ensures that the reinsured does not alter its underwriting practice for the business covered by the treaty without the reinsurers' prior agreement.
